CODE
Art. 2.3.55.
Preciput
The spouses may agree that the surviving spouse, or one of them if he or she survives, shall have the right to take from the common patrimony before any partition, either a certain sum, or certain assets in kind, or a certain quantity or share of a given type of property.
However, the benefits granted are considered to be a gift, up to a limit of half, if they relate to present or future property which the predeceased spouse has included in the common patrimony by express stipulation in the matrimonial agreement.
Property subject to preciput may be seized to pay joint debts, except, where the preciput relates to property in kind, the recourse of the beneficiary spouse to the remainder of the joint estate.
Such recourse may also be exercised in the event of the alienation by one of the spouses of property in kind which is the subject of the preciput.
